name: Rain
current_role: Likely Rainer (Reiner) Schmidt-Ruthenbeck, co-owner with brother Michael of the family's Metro AG stake
profile: Entry appears to be a truncated 'Rainer Schmidt-Ruthenbeck' (Germany, listed jointly with brother Michael). Born 1941, son of Metro co-founder Wilhelm Schmidt-Ruthenbeck; the brothers' family holding owned roughly 13-16% of German retailer Metro AG. Lives in Duisburg; keeps a very low profile.
interesting_fact: Forbes ranked Michael and Reiner Schmidt-Ruthenbeck jointly at #722 on its 2016 billionaires list with US$2.4 billion.
deep_cut_fact: His family (the Karl Schmidt family of Duisburg merchants) set up Stiftung Mercator in 1996, one of Germany's largest private foundations, named after the cartographer Gerhard Mercator, who lived in Duisburg for decades.
notes: Identity inferred: input name 'Rain' with shared_with 'Schmidt-Ruthenbeck Bros., Michael' (Forbes 1997) most likely = Rainer Schmidt-Ruthenbeck. Extremely private; no personal channels. The only route is via the family foundation (Stiftung Mercator), and it is indirect.

name: Raja Bagmane
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Bagmane Group (Bagmane Developers Pvt Ltd), Bengaluru
profile: Bengaluru real-estate developer who founded Bagmane Group in 1996 and built it into one of the city's largest commercial/tech-park landlords (Bagmane Tech Park, Bagmane World Technology Center; ~30 mn sq ft operational). Blackstone took a minority stake in 2024, and the group sponsors Bagmane Prime Office REIT, which has listed in India. His sons Aditya and Shashank are directors.
interesting_fact: Bagmane Tech Park in C V Raman Nagar, launched in 2001, was one of Bengaluru's earliest IT parks; the group's portfolio is now hosted in a Blackstone-backed listed REIT.
notes: Low media profile; rarely gives interviews. The published email is a general company enquiries inbox. A data-center/tech-park angle is relevant: Bagmane hosts big tech occupiers in Bengaluru. His sons may be easier to reach for a conversation.

name: Jose Batista Sobrinho
current_role: Founder of JBS S.A. (honorary patriarch; no operational role since the 1980s apart from a stint as interim CEO in 2017)
profile: 'Zé Mineiro' (b. 1933, Carmo do Rio Claro, Minas Gerais) opened a small butcher shop, Casa de Carnes Mineira, in Anápolis, Goiás, in 1953. It grew into JBS, named after his initials and now the world's largest meat processor, run by his sons Joesley and Wesley. In June 2025 he rang the NYSE opening bell for JBS's US listing.
interesting_fact: At around 91, he rang the opening bell at the New York Stock Exchange on 25 June 2025 when JBS began trading in New York, with his sons alongside him.
deep_cut_fact: His business first took off by selling beef to the construction companies building the new capital, Brasília, in the late 1950s. That was the springboard for what became JBS.
notes: He is in his 90s and has no public channels of his own. Any approach would go through JBS/J&F press. Hurun last listed him separately in 2014; the family wealth is mostly attributed to his sons.

name: Peter Hargreaves
current_role: Co-founder of Hargreaves Lansdown; backer/partner of Blue Whale Capital (left HL board Oct 2025; son Robert took his seat)
profile: Clitheroe-born chartered accountant who co-founded Hargreaves Lansdown with Stephen Lansdown from a Bristol spare bedroom in 1981, building the UK's largest retail investment platform. HL was taken private in a £5.4bn takeover in 2025, and he remains a major shareholder. He seeded fund manager Blue Whale Capital in 2017 and is the main stakeholder in satellite ground-station firm GomSpace.
interesting_fact: He came ninth among the UK's biggest taxpayers in 2021, with a reported tax bill of £91.4 million that year.
deep_cut_fact: An early backer of hydrogen: he joined the board of electrolyser maker ITM Power as a non-executive director in 2004, invested heavily, and recruited Dr Graham Cooley as its CEO in 2009. Before HL, he worked as a computer salesman.

public_contacts.value: Edelman Smithfield (Blue Whale Capital press): bluewhale@edelmansmithfield.com

notes: Outspoken and interview-friendly in the UK financial press. His energy and space investments (ITM Power hydrogen, GomSpace satellites) fit the podcast's angle. Blue Whale is the best route to him. Brexit donations are politically sensitive, so avoid leading with them.

name: Geoffrey Kwok
current_role: Director, Empire Group Holdings (Hong Kong); Non-Executive Director, Sun Hung Kai Properties
profile: Eldest son of the late Walter Kwok (ex-chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties) and grandson of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng. He studied economics at Yale, earned a Stanford MBA and worked as a Morgan Stanley investment banker. After his father died in 2018, he and his brother Jonathan took over Empire Group Holdings, which has invested over HK$29bn in property since 2010. He also joined the SHKP board.
interesting_fact: Empire Group's 'E' logomark is derived from Walter Kwok's own signature; the rest of the word 'Empire' is meant to be completed by the succeeding generation.
deep_cut_fact: The family's Walter & Wendy Kwok Family Foundation has donated to Hong Kong's Foodlink Foundation (hot meals, food waste from hotels) since 2011. Empire also runs a Kwok Scholars programme for tertiary students and opened Kimpton Tsim Sha Tsui in March 2026.
notes: Low profile. Empire Group is the more direct route, because SHKP press is controlled by the other branch of the family. Avoid the family-feud history.

name: Satyanarayana Chava
profile: Organic chemist (PhD) who spent about a decade in pharma, at Ranbaxy and then at Matrix Labs, where he rose to COO. He founded Laurus Labs in Hyderabad in 2005 as an R&D firm. It now supplies APIs and formulations for HIV, cancer, asthma and diabetes drugs and has expanded into CDMO and biotech. He still spends about 25% of his time in the labs.
interesting_fact: He is a named co-inventor on about 145 patents granted to Laurus Labs, and in his spare time he enjoys cooking Indian food and sweets.
deep_cut_fact: As founder and first employee he never held 50% of Laurus Labs. In 2006, a year after founding, he set aside 5% of the company's equity for employee stock options.
notes: He won EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2021 (Life Sciences & Healthcare category), and he serves on the USP board of trustees. I found no dedicated press email; the secretarial inbox is the published investor channel.

name: Sol Zakay
profile: Israeli-born British property investor (b. 1952) who founded Topland Group with his brother Eddie in the early 1990s (incorporated 1991). Topland made its name on large sale-and-leaseback deals with M&S, Tesco, Sainsbury's, Aldi and Eroski (over £1.5bn in 2000-10). It then expanded into hotels (exited 2019), bridging finance and development, and now has a £0.8bn development pipeline.
interesting_fact: Topland describes itself as a pioneer of UK alternative real-estate lending. It was also an original aggregator of UK supported-living housing, building a portfolio before selling to long-term holders including Civitas.
deep_cut_fact: In the 2010s Topland moved beyond property into renewable-energy investment alongside its real-estate activities. That history fits the podcast's energy angle well.
notes: Very private, with no social accounts. The Topland website has a 'Contact Sol' form on the People page, which is the most direct published route. The company has a past legal dispute with the UK Ministry of Justice (2012); do not raise it.

name: Patrice Pichet
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO (PDG), Groupe Pichet (Pessac, Gironde)
profile: Bordeaux-born (1959) property developer who started as a salesman for home-builder Maisons Phénix in 1983. He did his first property deal on a Bordeaux plot in 1988 and founded his own developer, Eurobat. Renamed Groupe Pichet in 2004, the family company now develops housing and commercial property across France, especially Île-de-France, and employs about 1,250-1,400 people.
interesting_fact: Groupe Pichet bought Château Les Carmes Haut-Brion (Pessac-Léognan) in 2010; it is the only Bordeaux château with an address inside the city of Bordeaux.
deep_cut_fact: He commissioned Philippe Starck (with architect Luc Arsène-Henry) to design a ship-shaped winery at Les Carmes Haut-Brion. Inaugurated in 2016 at a cost of about €10m, it was the first wine cellar of Starck's career.
notes: French-language outreach is advisable. The Groupe Pichet press office is the best route; the wine estate (les-carmes-haut-brion.com) is a softer conversational hook.

name: Hayes Barnard
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, GoodLeap; Founder and Chairman, GivePower Foundation
profile: St. Louis-area native and former Oracle sales executive. He founded Paramount Equity Mortgage in 2003 and Paramount Solar in 2008, sold the solar unit to SolarCity, and was SolarCity's chief revenue officer. Back at his own firm, he turned it into Loanpal/GoodLeap, a point-of-sale platform that has financed over $26bn of solar and other green home upgrades and was valued at $12bn in 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2014 he founded the nonprofit GivePower, which builds solar-powered clean water and energy systems, including solar desalination, for underserved communities worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: He won a football scholarship to Central Missouri State but was injured as a freshman and transferred to Mizzou. On arriving in San Francisco in 1995 for the tech boom, his first jobs were staffing booths at trade shows.
notes: He is a strong fit for an energy podcast: residential solar finance, an ex-SolarCity executive, and GivePower solar water projects. He is publicly visible and does interviews; GoodLeap press is the best route.

name: Liu Xianbing
current_role: Listed by Hurun as the principal behind 'Kema Tech' (manufacturing); title not verified
profile: Chinese manufacturing entrepreneur (刘先兵) listed on the Hurun China (2024-26) and Hurun Global (2025-26) rich lists with about US$2.75bn, attributed to 'Kema Tech'. I could not verify the company's full name, his role or his biography from accessible public sources in this pass.
notes: Not researched in depth: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry, and Wikipedia has no article on him or on 'Kema Tech'. Needs a follow-up pass with Chinese-language sources (Hurun detail page, exchange filings for the Kema entity) to confirm identity and find an IR contact.

name: Chao Teng-hsiung
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder, Farglory Group (Farglory Land); son Frank Chao has chaired Farglory Land since 2014
profile: Born in 1944 in Houlong, Miaoli, Taiwan, into a poor family. He moved to Taipei and saved from odd jobs to supply cement to builders before developing his own factory-office buildings. He started in property in 1969, founded what became Farglory Land in 1978 and grew Farglory Group into a conglomerate spanning real estate, life insurance, hotels, air-cargo logistics and Hualien's Farglory Ocean Park.
interesting_fact: After junior high school, he started out as an apprentice in concrete formwork and masonry, the trade he later scaled into one of Taiwan's largest developers.
deep_cut_fact: Working with sculptor Ju Ming, he backed a 2011 arrangement letting primary-school children from Taipei and New Taipei visit the Juming Museum free all year round; then-Taipei mayor Hau Lung-bin praised him for it.
notes: Sensitive: he was convicted at first instance in 2022 in a bribery case (Taipei Dome/Farglory), with appeals ongoing per Forbes. Approach is likely unrealistic; any outreach should go via Farglory corporate IR. Mandarin is required.

name: Tom Ford
current_role: Film director, writer and producer (Fade to Black); founder of Tom Ford International (sold to Estée Lauder, 2022)
profile: Texas-born designer who revived Gucci as creative director (1994-2004) and founded Tom Ford International in 2005. He sold the brand and its beauty business to Estée Lauder for $2.8bn in 2022 and stepped back fully at the end of 2023. He is now focused on film: after A Single Man and Nocturnal Animals, he is directing an adaptation of Anne Rice's Cry to Heaven, which began shooting in January 2026.
interesting_fact: He trained in interior architecture at Parsons rather than fashion. His Santa Fe ranch, Cerro Pelon, was designed by Japanese architect Tadao Ando.
deep_cut_fact: To land his first fashion job, he phoned designer Cathy Hardwick every day for a month. Asked his favourite European designers, he said 'Armani and Chanel', later admitting it was because she was wearing Armani. He worked as her design assistant for two years.
notes: No personal channels found; the Tom Ford brand accounts are now owned by Estée Lauder, not by him. The most realistic route is via his film company Fade to Black or his film publicists around the Cry to Heaven release. He is a weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Thomas Steyer
current_role: Co-founder and co-executive chair, Galvanize Climate Solutions; 2026 California gubernatorial candidate (finished third in the June 2026 primary)
profile: Founded hedge fund Farallon Capital and ran it for 26 years before selling out in 2012 to focus on climate and politics. He founded NextGen Climate/America and ran for president in 2020. In 2021 he co-founded climate investor Galvanize with Katie Hall. He spent heavily on a 2026 run for California governor but placed third in the June primary and did not advance.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he and his wife Kat Taylor gave $41m to create the TomKat Center for Sustainable Energy at Stanford. In 2024 he published a climate book, 'Cheaper, Faster, Better: How We'll Win the Climate War'.
deep_cut_fact: He and Kat Taylor run TomKat Ranch in Pescadero, near Half Moon Bay, a working cattle ranch used to research and demonstrate regenerative, climate-friendly agriculture. The New York Times called it 'an accidental cattle ranch'.
notes: He is an excellent fit for an energy podcast (climate investing, energy research philanthropy, and a climate-economics book) and is very media-accessible. Galvanize media contact is the best route. Since he is fresh off a losing governor campaign, lead with energy and investing, not politics.

name: Serge Godin
current_role: Founder and co-chair of the board, CGI Inc. (daughter Julie Godin became executive chair in 2025)
profile: One of nine children from a Lac-Saint-Jean sawmill family. He studied computing and administration, then used $5,000 of savings to found CGI in Quebec City in 1976 at age 26. He was CEO until 2006 and grew CGI through 100+ acquisitions (including Bell Sygma in 1998) into a C$15bn-revenue global IT services and consulting firm. His family office, Distinction Capital, manages family capital and the Fondation Famille Godin.
interesting_fact: After his father's uninsured sawmill burned down, the young Godin worked at a convenience store after school and at a dry cleaner's on Saturdays to help pay the family's bills.
deep_cut_fact: He earned one of the first CEGEP diplomas in computer science ever awarded in Quebec, at the Collège de Jonquière. His family office, Distinction Capital, is based in Montreal's 1906 heritage William Alexander Molson house.
notes: French-language outreach is preferred. The family office email is the most direct published route; otherwise go through CGI media relations (cgi.com). CGI's IT services and data-center outsourcing fit the podcast's theme.

name: Alfred West Jr
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, SEI Investments (retired as executive chairman and left the board 1 Jan 2026)
profile: Founded SEI (Simulated Environments Inc.) in 1968, beginning with a computer simulation to train bank loan officers. He took it public in 1981 and grew it into a fintech, investment-processing and asset-management firm that manages, advises or administers about $1.8-2.1 trillion. He was CEO for 54 years until 2022, then executive chairman, and became chairman emeritus in January 2026.
interesting_fact: He wanted to be a fighter pilot and studied aerospace engineering at Georgia Tech, but poor eyesight kept him from flying, so he took a Wharton MBA and launched SEI instead.
deep_cut_fact: SEI's first product was the industry's first computer-based commercial credit simulator. In the 1970s it pivoted to an automated trust-accounting system that became TRUST 3000, the platform behind its move into fintech.
notes: Recently retired (Dec 2025 announcement), so a 'founder's 57-year journey' angle is timely. The SEI media contact is the most practical route.

name: Marc Lasry
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Avenue Capital Group
profile: Born in Marrakesh, he moved to the US at age 7. A bankruptcy lawyer turned distressed-debt investor, he co-founded Amroc Investments (1989) and Avenue Capital (1995, with $7m) with his sister Sonia Gardner; Avenue manages about $13bn in distressed and undervalued credit. He co-owned the Milwaukee Bucks from 2014 to 2023 and in 2026 was a finalist bidder for a potential NBA Las Vegas expansion team.
interesting_fact: In September 2026 his group, with Steve Apostolopoulos, was one of three finalists bidding for a potential NBA expansion franchise in Las Vegas. He also sold a Wonder Woman #1 comic for a record $291,000 in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in the bankruptcy practice of law firm Angel & Frankel. He first got into buying trade claims of bankrupt companies as head of private debt at the small firm R.D. Smith, the niche that became Amroc and then Avenue. In 2013 he declined consideration as US ambassador to France.

public_contacts.value: Kekst and Company, Todd Fogarty: todd-fogarty@kekst.com (Avenue media relations)

notes: Media-friendly and a frequent CNBC guest. The best route is Kekst (Avenue's media relations). Avenue's site says only business-related communications are forwarded to staff.

name: Lin Tengjiao
current_role: Founder and chairman/CEO, Yango Longjing Group (Yango Holdings), Fuzhou (current status not verified)
profile: Fujian-born (1968, Minhou) Peking University graduate who studied in Singapore, then returned to Fuzhou in 1995 to found Yango Education. He built Yango into a conglomerate spanning property (Yango Group, Shenzhen-listed from 2002), finance, environmental protection (Longking), education and trading. He has been a delegate to the 12th and 13th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: He bought the listed shell Shishi Xinfa for about RMB 50.8m in 2002 and renamed it Yango Group (阳光城), which became one of China's top-20 developers by sales before the 2021-22 property downturn.
deep_cut_fact: His business empire started with education, not property: after returning from study in Singapore in 1995, his first venture in Fuzhou was 'Yango Education' (阳光教育). Property development followed in 1996.
notes: Dropped off Hurun lists after 2022 following Yango Group's debt default. Treat his wealth and status as uncertain and avoid the subject. The group website returned an empty page in this pass, and no published contact email was found. The Longking environmental and energy unit is a possible podcast angle. A Mandarin-language approach is required.
